# Cartridge: system and authoring guide

Cartridge hosts replaceable Lua and SDK process cartridges. Start here, then
read the linked plain-text guides relevant to the task. Paths are relative to
this source repository.

- [Writing good modules](docs/writing-good-modules.txt): useful events, direct
  integration, cartridge dependencies, and documentation through memo tools.
- [Documentation discovery](../docs.ctg/.cartridge/memos/note/documentation-service.md):
  find documentation across repositories with the docs service and docs.available event.
- [System architecture](docs/architecture.txt): repository layout, runtime,
  dependency resolution, processes, replacement, permissions, and cartridge roles.
- [Creating cartridges](docs/creating-cartridges.txt): complete Lua example,
  Rust SDK adapter, manifest fields, registration, profiles, and validation.
- [Development and operation](docs/development.txt): build/test selection,
  proxy, MCP registration, local data, Git workflow, and troubleshooting.
- [Memos and knowledge](docs/memos.txt): record types, validated writes,
  discovery, system prompts, and the cartridge-creation routine.

The executable declaration belongs in each cartridge.json. It includes purpose,
services, dependencies, grants, and documented command argument arrays. Reading
commands does not execute them. Memos hold context, decisions, and procedures.
There is no separate development JSON.

A good cartridge owns a concrete capability, exposes useful state changes as
events, and calls declared dependencies directly for required results. Reuse the
system's services and preserve their context, errors, and lifecycle. Keep service
and event contracts discoverable in memos alongside the implementation.

The guides describe this checkout, not a promise that unfinished sandbox work
is complete. Source contracts and tests are authoritative when behavior changes.
See src/loader.rs for the manifest schema.
